title: MsspProvider.status only accepts the 5 defined lifecycle values and organizationId is unique
description: mssp-provider.model.js: status enum ['provisioning','active','suspended','deowned','provisioning_failed'], default 'provisioning'; organizationId is required+unique — an organization can never have two MsspProvider documents.
steps: Attempt to save an MsspProvider with status="pending" (not in the enum)
Attempt to save a second MsspProvider for an organizationId that already has one
expectedResult: Both attempts fail Mongoose validation/the unique index; only enum-listed statuses are ever persisted and only one MsspProvider can exist per organization.

title: MsspClientRelationship.clientOrgId has a plain (non-partial) unique index — a detached client can never receive a second relationship document, by any provider
description: mssp-client-relationship.model.js line 8: clientOrgId: { unique:true } with no partialFilterExpression, unlike TenantInvitation's targetOrgId+email index which is deliberately partial on status:'pending'. Because 'detached' relationships are never deleted, once a client organization has ANY relationship row (even a long-detached one) it structurally cannot be re-onboarded as a managed client again — not by the original provider, and not by a different one — since MsspClientRelationship.create() would violate the unique index. This is a real, verified structural limitation worth confirming is intentional.
preconditions: A client organization has a MsspClientRelationship document with status="detached"
steps: Attempt POST /mssp/clients (or a raw MsspClientRelationship.create) for that same clientOrgId under a new or the same provider
expectedResult: The insert fails with a MongoDB duplicate-key error on the clientOrgId unique index — a formerly-managed, detached client organization can never become an MSSP-managed client again through the current data model. Flag this as a gap/limitation to confirm with product: there is no re-attach flow.

title: MsspFrameworkLicense.frameworkCode is always normalized to lowercase/trimmed at the schema level
description: mssp-framework-license.model.js line 9: frameworkCode: { type:String, required:true, trim:true, lowercase:true } — this normalization is what makes resolveLicensedFrameworks()'s case-insensitive code matching (tenant-provisioning.service.js lines 292,309) safe.
steps: Save an MsspFrameworkLicense with frameworkCode=" ISO27001 " (mixed case, padded)
expectedResult: The persisted document's frameworkCode is exactly "iso27001".

title: MsspAuditEvent is schema-enforced append-only: no updatedAt field exists, and actorType is restricted to 4 values
description: mssp-audit-event.model.js line 20: timestamps:{createdAt:true, updatedAt:false} — there is no updatedAt path on the schema at all, so no application code path can silently 'edit' an existing audit event's timestamp. actorType enum is ['platform','mssp','customer','system']; actorType/actorId/action are required.
steps: Inspect the compiled MsspAuditEvent schema paths for an updatedAt field
Attempt to save an MsspAuditEvent with actorType="support" (not in the enum)
expectedResult: No updatedAt schema path exists on MsspAuditEvent. The actorType="support" save fails validation.

title: TenantInvitation.type only accepts the 5 defined invitation classifications
description: invitation.model.js line 17: type enum ['direct_owner','mssp_owner','mssp_employee','mssp_client_user','customer_user']. A new invitation classification introduced without updating this enum would fail fast at save time instead of silently miscategorizing the invitation.
steps: Attempt to save a TenantInvitation with type="mssp_admin" (not defined)
expectedResult: The save is rejected by Mongoose enum validation.

title: ProvisioningOperation.idempotencyKey is globally unique and type/status are restricted to their defined enums
description: provisioning-operation.model.js: idempotencyKey required+unique (line 7); type enum ['direct_onboarding','mssp_onboarding','mssp_client_onboarding']; status enum ['processing','complete','failed','compensating'], default 'processing'.
steps: Save two ProvisioningOperation documents with the same idempotencyKey
expectedResult: The duplicate-key save fails on the unique index; the invalid-type save fails enum validation.

title: OwnershipTransfer requires reason and requestedBy, and status is restricted to its 4-value lifecycle
description: ownership-transfer.model.js: reason and requestedBy are required (lines 10-11); status enum ['previewed','processing','complete','failed'], default 'previewed' — matching detachClient's create-then-update-to-complete/failed pattern (admin.controller.js lines 639-663).
steps: Attempt to save an OwnershipTransfer with no reason field
Attempt to save one with status="cancelled" (not defined)

title: resolveLicensedFrameworks() short-circuits to an empty array for an empty/undefined request and throws forbidden listing exact missing codes otherwise
description: tenant-provisioning.service.js resolveLicensedFrameworks() (lines 290-318): line 291 returns [] immediately without a DB query when requested is empty/not an array; otherwise any requested value not resolvable to an active, in-date, licensed MsspFrameworkLicense throws AppError.forbidden naming every missing value.
expectedResult: Call 1 returns [] without touching MsspFrameworkLicense. Call 2 throws AppError.forbidden with a message that names "pci-dss" as outside the catalog (and does not falsely also name "iso27001").
